title: Grateful Dead Live at Berkeley Community Theater on 1972-08-24
lineage: SBD>Rm>Dat(48k) with missing songs patched  from SBD>Rm>Cass>Cass>Cass>Dat>Samplitude>SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording of a high‑energy Berkeley show highlighted by a smoking Dark Star→Morning Dew and a rollicking Half Step.
ai_review.review: The August 24, 1972 Berkeley performance is widely praised for its soaring second set – especially the near‑perfect Dark Star into Morning Dew and an exuberant Half Step that kicks off the night. The Charlie Miller SBD remaster delivers crystal‑clear balance with only minor vocal‑level quirks, making it a top‑tier listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews, the vast majority rate the show 4–5 stars and extol both the musical performance and the soundboard mix; only a few minor complaints appear.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Remastered SBD is crisp, well‑balanced and “well‑balanced for an SBD”; occasional comments about vocals being a bit loud but no major dropouts or muddiness.

poor_songs: Greatest Story (vocals a bit harsh for some listeners)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Set sequencing is praised as pure genius, with a tight first set and a second‑set that builds to an intense Dark Star/Dew climax before a sweet encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for his rollicking Half Step and overall strong guitar tone throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as “in top form” with notable bass flourishes (e.g., boop‑booping in Sugaree) and leading the Dark Star transition.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted as sounding great, especially on rhythm parts; several reviewers call out his solid playing.
